items.title: Harold Dejan Interview, 1960-10-14
items.q: Well, it was Willa McG Rogers, I think. And we used to stand in front of the school and wait until we come and buy them to school and even walk home together.

ctx.x: I won't say dinner there. They must not have had segregation those days. What? That's when Bunk Johnson first came to town. Well, I tell you now, a long time ago,

things were mighty nice around town. That was 1942. I always did go hours ago. I mean, because I know how to care of myself and take care of myself. But I mean, people didn't go all foolish like that. People are foolish, you know. We used to have some boys across the street at my house. The boys would start playing saxophone. My brother and I was playing music and live across the street at my house. We used to go to school together every morning. We used to stand, just carve a school around on the Man Street.…
